Package edu.ucsb.cs.citelines.services

Record Class ResolvedWork

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
edu.ucsb.cs.citelines.services.ResolvedWork
public record ResolvedWork(String id, String doi, String title, Integer year, String type, List<String> authorNames, String venue, List<String> referencedWorkIds, List<ResolvedWork> embeddedReferences, List<ResolvedWork> embeddedCitations, String abstractText, String publisher, String pages, String isbn, String series, String address, String volume, String number) extends Record
A minimal, resolver-agnostic projection of a scholarly work, carrying only the fields BibTexSynthesisService needs to synthesize a BibTeX entry, plus enough of its reference/citation graph for CitationGraphService to discover related works without a second round-trip where a resolver's API already hands them over in the same response.

id is the resolving CitationMetadataResolver's own native id for this work (e.g. an OpenAlex id like "W3035965352", with any URL prefix already stripped) — ids are only meaningful within the resolver that produced them, never compared across resolvers. doi, by contrast, is always normalized (via DOIService.normalizeRawDOI(java.lang.String)) so it can be compared across resolvers for deduplication.

referencedWorkIds holds native ids that still need a same-resolver follow-up fetch to hydrate (OpenAlex's two-step id-list-then-batch-fetch shape). embeddedReferences/ embeddedCitations hold related works that arrived already fully hydrated in the same response that resolved this work (Crossref's inline reference array, Semantic Scholar's inline references/citations fields) — a resolver populates at most one of referencedWorkIds or embeddedReferences, never both. All three list fields are always non-null (an empty List.of() when not applicable) — every CitationMetadataResolver implementation is expected to uphold this, since callers rely on it.

abstractText, publisher, pages, isbn, series, address, volume, and number are best-effort: not every resolver's API exposes all of them (see each resolver's own parsing for which it populates), so BibTexSynthesisService treats every one of these as optional. (abstractText, not abstract, since the latter is a Java reserved word.)
